summary.intent: Finalize performance measurements for caliper main after a batch of merged PRs, then restructure the remaining agent-driven work to cut human-style ceremony (relaying, re-describing, per-branch bookkeeping) and start the remaining tasks under that model.
summary.outcome: Reported final perf numbers (about 1.26s/955MiB on gate-large and 0.92s/695MiB on Chakra-only with the checker, roughly 4-6x faster than RDT, with reruns near 0.18s). Wrote a 385-word worker contract, launched two Sonnet workers (pipeline overlap F9/F11, and JSDoc bug plus weekly alias pairing) with short briefs, and set up a single status command across open PRs.

repo: Rust 1.99.1 must be on PATH for builds, and commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 because the mise shim forces 1.98.1; with the toolchain bin first on PATH, rust-objcopy can fail and strip silently does nothing.
CI runs deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration and test-py on every PR, so workers only run lint/doc-check/machete/typos plus targeted checks for what they touched.

Output-preserving changes are verified by a full-content JSON diff (stats dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against an origin/main build on the gate-large and chakra-only fixtures; tools live in caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis (same.py, identity.sh) and final-perf/ab.sh interleaves two binaries.

Entire findings are listed with `entire trail finding list --branch <b> --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --project gh/orin-dx`; a finding stays 'open, current' until Entire re-reviews, even after the fix is pushed.
Subagents receive CLAUDE.md automatically, so the worker contract belongs there instead of being repeated in each brief.
workflow: Machine load of 5-30 (from CI, other sessions and about 20 cold Rust rebuilds) makes wall-clock timings only ±0.1s reliable; prefer allocation or instruction counts, and interleave A/B runs.
Short briefs (about 150 words) pointing to a shared contract replace 800-1500 word briefs; workers write the PR body to a file and the lead publishes it unedited.
Run one status command (state, failing checks, findings across all open PRs) only on events instead of polling.
Stacked PRs and manual trail linking caused mistakes like the #444 merge landing in the wrong branch.

friction: Stacked-PR merge for #444 landed in the wrong branch.
Heavy machine load from many workers each cold-building Rust (60-70s each).

The #455 worker's tests only partly ran against the old logic (the reverse arrangement never ran because the test stopped at the first failure), and it read the checker-lane result from piped output rather than an exit code.
Findings had to be relayed manually from the user to workers, and worker reports were rewritten several times.
Gate measurement numbers for Storybook first answer vary (115ms vs 159ms), and watch p95 of about 164ms is far over the 25ms budget.
open_items: #455 needs CI confirmation and verification of the symlink fix (head 5b1c9777); release PR #396 awaits the user.
Wait for the two running workers (perf/overlap-extract-stages and fix/jsdoc-and-weekly-pairing) to report.
Move the worker contract into the repo's CLAUDE.md.
Build the finding-routing scheduled check, a CI golden check (canonical output hash, allocation count, determinism), a shared build cache, a merge queue, and per-goal umbrella trails.
Check whether Callisto 0.20 can infer versions from conventional commits and whether a merge queue fits the Entire gates.
Storybook live-upgrade and S7b are held; the oracle run is the user's call on cost.
Re-measure Storybook first-answer and watch latency on a quiet machine.
Re-run RDT for a precise ratio, since the current ratios use earlier RDT numbers.
